guide.summary: 被 puts the thing affected first and the doer second: Receiver + 被 + doer + verb + what happened to it. The sentence is about the receiver and how it ended up, so the verb has to carry a result or 了, exactly as in a 把 sentence turned around. Chinese uses 被 far less than English uses 'was done': when a thing obviously cannot act by itself, the plain sentence (作业写完了) is already passive.

subs.label: Receiver + 被 + doer + verb
subs.focus: Force the order: receiver before 被, doer right after 被, all of it before the verb. Classic errors: 被 + doer after the verb like English 'by ...' (手机偷走了被小偷), or doer and receiver swapped. Make 被 and the doer separate tiles; in cloze, offer 把 and 给 as distractors.

subs.label: 被 with no doer; 被人
subs.focus: Decide whether the doer can be left out. After 被 it can (钱包被偷了), or use 人 for an unknown doer. After 叫/让 a doer is required: 让偷了 is wrong, 让人偷了 is right. Cloze: 被 against 叫/让 with no doer following. Judge: 叫/让 directly before the verb (wrong), 被 directly before the verb (correct trap).

subs.label: 没, 不会, 已经, 别 go before 被
subs.focus: Place 没, 不会, 会, 可能, 已经, 也, 都, 别 before 被, never between the doer and the verb. Also: a past event is negated with 没(有)被, not 不被, and 没 drops the final 了. Classic errors: 被没偷, 被老师会批评, 没被偷了. Make the negator or modal its own tile.

subs.label: The verb cannot stand bare
subs.focus: A one-syllable verb cannot end a 被 sentence alone: it needs a result (完, 走, 坏, 破, 开), a direction, 到 + place, 得 + description, or at least 了. Classic error: 蛋糕被弟弟吃. Cloze: complement or 了 against ∅. Never mark a bare two-syllable verb after a modal as wrong (会被批评 is fine).

subs.label: Spoken 叫 / 让 for 被
subs.focus: Recognise 叫/让 as spoken passive markers: same order as 被, doer always stated (自行车让人骑走了). Keep it apart from 让/叫 'let, tell to': subject is the thing affected and the verb has a result. Errors: dropping the doer, reading 让 as 'let'. Never offer 被 and 叫/让 together when both fit.

subs.label: Passive without 被
subs.focus: Leave 被 out when a thing that cannot act is the subject, no doer is named and nothing bad happened: 作业写完了, 饭做好了. Error: 被 for every English 'was done'. The 被 version is odd, not impossible, so use cloze (被 vs ∅, cue asks for the natural sentence), 被 as an extra tile, or correct judge items only.

subs.label: 把 ⇄ 被 conversion
subs.focus: Convert both ways: 把 object becomes 被 subject, 把 subject becomes the doer after 被, everything from the verb on is unchanged, negation and modals stay before 把/被. Errors: keeping 把 inside the 被 sentence, losing the result. Mostly rewrite items; for 被 to 把 the source must name a doer.

rules.rule: Start with the thing or person affected, then 被, then who did it, then the verb with its result. The 被 phrase always comes before the verb.
rules.pattern: Receiver + 被 + Doer + Verb + result / 了

examples.zh: 我的手机被小偷偷走了。
examples.py: wǒ de shǒu jī bèi xiǎo tōu tōu zǒu le
examples.en: My phone was stolen by a thief.

examples.py: dàn gāo bèi dì di chī wán le
examples.en: The cake was finished off by my little brother.

examples.py: nà běn shū bèi xiǎo wáng jiè zǒu le
examples.en: That book was borrowed by Xiao Wang.

rules.note: 被 is most at home with things that are unwelcome for the receiver (stolen, broken, scolded), but neutral and good events are also normal in modern Chinese, especially in writing.

rules.rule: If you do not know or do not care who did it, put the verb right after 被, or use 人 for 'someone'.
rules.pattern: Receiver + 被 + (人) + Verb + result / 了

examples.py: wǒ de qián bāo bèi tōu le
examples.en: My wallet was stolen.

examples.py: bēi zi bèi dǎ pò le
examples.en: The cup got broken.

examples.py: wǒ de sǎn bèi rén ná zǒu le
examples.en: Someone took my umbrella.

rules.note: Only 被 can do this. 叫 and 让 must be followed by a doer, even if it is just 人.

rules.rule: Negatives, modal verbs and adverbs go in front of 被. For something that did not happen use 没 or 没有, and leave out 了.
rules.pattern: Receiver + 没 / 不会 / 已经 / 也 + 被 + (Doer) + Verb + result

examples.zh: 还好，我的钱包没被偷走。
examples.py: hái hǎo wǒ de qián bāo méi bèi tōu zǒu
examples.en: Luckily my wallet wasn't stolen.

examples.zh: 你这样做会被老师批评的。
examples.py: nǐ zhè yàng zuò huì bèi lǎo shī pī píng de
examples.en: You'll be criticised by the teacher if you do that.

examples.zh: 放心，我们不会被发现的。
examples.py: fàng xīn wǒ men bù huì bèi fā xiàn de
examples.en: Don't worry, we won't be found out.

examples.py: dàn gāo yǐ jīng bèi chī wán le
examples.en: The cake has already been eaten up.

rules.note: 不被 exists, but for general or habitual statements (他不被大家理解, 'he is not understood by people'), not for a single past event.

rules.rule: To warn someone, put 别 before 被.
rules.pattern: 别 + 被 + Doer + Verb + 了 / result

examples.py: bié bèi tā piàn le
examples.en: Don't let him fool you.

examples.zh: 小声点儿，别被老师发现了。
examples.py: xiǎo shēng diǎn r bié bèi lǎo shī fā xiàn le
examples.en: Keep your voice down, don't let the teacher catch us.

rules.rule: After the verb, say how things ended up: a result word, a direction, 到 + place, or at least 了. A bare one-syllable verb cannot end the sentence.
rules.pattern: Receiver + 被 + (Doer) + Verb + 完 / 走 / 坏 / 开 / 到… + 了

examples.py: chuāng hu bèi fēng chuī kāi le
examples.en: The window was blown open by the wind.

examples.py: wǒ de yī fu bèi nòng zāng le
examples.en: My clothes got dirty.

examples.py: tā bèi sòng dào yī yuàn qù le
examples.en: He was taken to hospital.

rules.note: Two-syllable verbs are freer: after a modal or in formal style they can stand alone (会被批评, 被发现). For a finished single event they still take 了 or a result.

rules.rule: To describe the state something was left in, use Verb + 得 + description.
rules.pattern: Receiver + 被 + (Doer) + Verb + 得 + description

examples.py: fáng jiān bèi tā nòng de hěn luàn
examples.en: He left the room in a mess.

examples.zh: 我被他气得说不出话来。
examples.py: wǒ bèi tā qì de shuō bù chū huà lái
examples.en: He made me so angry I couldn't speak.

rules.rule: In everyday speech 叫 or 让 can replace 被. The order is the same, but the doer must be said.
rules.pattern: Receiver + 叫 / 让 + Doer + Verb + result / 了

examples.zh: 我的自行车让人骑走了。
examples.py: wǒ de zì xíng chē ràng rén qí zǒu le
examples.en: Someone rode off on my bike.

examples.py: dàn gāo jiào dì di chī guāng le
examples.en: My little brother ate all the cake.

examples.zh: 我的词典让小王借走了。
examples.py: wǒ de cí diǎn ràng xiǎo wáng jiè zǒu le
examples.en: My dictionary was borrowed by Xiao Wang.

rules.note: 让 and 叫 also mean 'let / tell someone to' (妈妈让我洗碗). It is passive when the subject is the thing affected and the verb has a result. In writing, use 被.

rules.rule: When the subject is a thing that plainly cannot do the action and you only report the result, use no 被 at all: thing + verb + result + 了.
rules.pattern: Thing + (已经 / 还没) + Verb + result + 了

examples.py: zuò yè xiě wán le
examples.en: The homework is done.

examples.py: fàn zuò hǎo le kuài lái chī ba
examples.en: Dinner is ready, come and eat.

examples.py: piào yǐ jīng mài wán le
examples.en: The tickets have already sold out.

examples.py: yī fu hái méi xǐ gān jìng
examples.en: The clothes haven't been washed clean yet.

rules.note: Adding 被 here is not strictly ungrammatical, but it sounds odd or suggests something unwanted. Use 被 when you name the doer, when something bad happened to the receiver, or when the subject is a person who could otherwise be taken as the doer (他打了 'he hit' against 他被打了 'he was hit').

rules.rule: 把 to 被: move the 把 object to the front, put the old subject after 被, and copy everything from the verb onward unchanged.
rules.pattern: Doer + 把 + Receiver + Verb + result  →  Receiver + 被 + Doer + Verb + result

examples.py: dì di bǎ dàn gāo chī wán le
examples.en: My little brother finished the cake.

examples.py: dàn gāo bèi dì di chī wán le
examples.en: The cake was finished by my little brother.

examples.py: fēng bǎ wǒ de mào zi chuī zǒu le
examples.en: The wind blew my hat away.

examples.py: wǒ de mào zi bèi fēng chuī zǒu le
examples.en: My hat was blown away by the wind.

rules.note: 把 and 被 never appear together for the same object in these sentences: pick one.

rules.rule: Negatives and modals keep their place in front: before 把 in the active sentence, before 被 in the passive one.
rules.pattern: Doer + 没 + 把 + Receiver + Verb + result  →  Receiver + 没 + 被 + Doer + Verb + result

examples.py: tā méi bǎ wǒ de chē kāi zǒu
examples.en: He didn't drive my car away.

examples.py: wǒ de chē méi bèi tā kāi zǒu
examples.en: My car wasn't driven away by him.

contrasts.wrong: 我的手机偷走了被小偷。

right.zh: 我的手机被小偷偷走了。
right.py: wǒ de shǒu jī bèi xiǎo tōu tōu zǒu le
right.en: My phone was stolen by a thief.

contrasts.why: English puts 'by a thief' at the end; Chinese puts 被 + doer before the verb.

right.py: dàn gāo bèi dì di chī wán le
right.en: The cake was eaten up by my little brother.

contrasts.why: A bare one-syllable verb cannot end a 被 sentence; say what became of the cake with a result or 了.

right.py: wǒ de qián bāo méi bèi tōu zǒu

contrasts.why: 没 goes before 被, not between 被 and the verb.

right.py: wǒ de qián bāo méi bèi tōu zǒu

contrasts.why: 没 says it did not happen, so the completion 了 is dropped.

right.py: tā huì bèi lǎo shī pī píng de
right.en: He will be criticised by the teacher.

contrasts.why: Modal verbs such as 会 go before 被, not after the doer.

right.zh: 我的自行车让人骑走了。
right.py: wǒ de zì xíng chē ràng rén qí zǒu le
right.en: Someone rode off on my bike.

contrasts.why: 让 and 叫 need a doer after them. With no doer use 被 (被骑走了) or add 人.

right.py: dàn gāo bèi dì di chī wán le
right.en: The cake was finished by my little brother.

contrasts.why: When turning 把 into 被, 把 disappears: its object has already moved to the front.

right.py: fàn zuò hǎo le kuài lái chī ba
right.en: Dinner is ready, come and eat.

contrasts.why: Unnatural rather than impossible: food cannot cook, nothing bad happened and no doer is named, so Chinese leaves 被 out.

cheat: Receiver first, then 被 + doer, then the verb. Never 被 + doer at the end.
Verb in a 被 sentence needs a tail: result, direction, 得 or 了.
没 / 不会 / 会 / 已经 / 别 all go before 被; with 没, drop 了.
No doer? 被 works alone. 叫 and 让 need at least 人.
Thing that cannot act + result, no doer, nothing bad: skip 被 (作业写完了).
把 → 被: swap the two nouns, keep everything from the verb onward, delete 把.
